title: A dub techno 12-inch
description: One track built from nothing, a lesson at a time: a pulse, a chord, echoes, space, movement, then the arrangement.
author: Strudel Workshop

tracks.title: A dub techno 12-inch
tracks.blurb: Every lesson starts from the code you finished in the one before, and the last one is the whole track.

lessons.title: The pulse
lessons.goal: Start the track: a steady 909 kick and quiet offbeat hats at 122 BPM.
lessons.concept:
Dub techno (Basic Channel, Maurizio, Deepchord) is **patience**: a steady pulse, one chord, and effects doing the storytelling over many minutes. We'll build one such track across this whole line of lessons; each lesson picks up the code where the last one left it.

It starts, as the records do, with the **pulse**: a four-on-the-floor kick and hats on the offbeats, kept quiet. Nothing here should be loud.
lessons.starter:
// A dub techno 12-inch. Tempo first:
setcpm(122/4)

tasks.text: Add a part called kick: a TR-909 kick on every beat.
tasks.hint: const kick = s("bd*4").bank("RolandTR909"), then play it with stack(kick).

tasks.text: Add a part called hats: closed hats on the offbeats, quiet.
tasks.hint: const hats = s("[~ hh]*4").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.35), and stack(kick, hats).

summary: Dub techno is a steady pulse with effects doing the work.
Four-on-the-floor kick, quiet offbeat hats, 120–124 BPM.

lessons.title: The chord
lessons.goal: Add the one chord the whole track lives on, dark and filtered.
lessons.concept:
A dub techno track usually has **one chord**, a minor seventh or ninth, played as a short stab and then drowned in effects. The chord is a sawtooth through a **low-pass filter**, closed down so it glows rather than shines.

`note("[c3,eb3,g3,bb3]")` plays four notes at once: C minor 7. `.struct("[~ x]*2")` makes it hit on the offbeats of 2 and 4, where the clap would be.

tasks.text: Add a part called stab: a C minor 7 chord on a sawtooth, hitting on the offbeats of 2 and 4, at gain .4.
tasks.hint: const stab = note("[c3,eb3,g3,bb3]").struct("[~ x]*2").s("sawtooth").gain(.4), and stack(kick, hats, stab).

tasks.text: Close the filter down to 800 Hz, and make the chord short: a quick decay and no sustain.

challenge.text: Add a little resonance so the filter sings.

summary: One minor-seventh chord, played as a short offbeat stab.
A closed low-pass filter makes it glow instead of shine.

lessons.title: The echo
lessons.goal: Send the chord into a dotted-eighth delay with long feedback.
lessons.concept:
The dub in dub techno is the **delay**. Each chord stab echoes in time with the beat, and with high **feedback** the echoes pile up into a wash that keeps moving after the stab is gone.

`.delaysync(3/16)` sets the echo time to a dotted eighth, the classic dub spacing. `.delayfeedback(.6)` is how much of each echo comes back round.

Strudel has one delay per **orbit**, so the stab gets its own: `.orbit(2)`. Anything else that wants a different delay later gets another orbit.

tasks.text: Give the stab a dotted-eighth delay with feedback of .6.
Put the stab on its own orbit, number 2, so its delay is its own.

challenge.text: Push the feedback up towards a wash: .75 or more (but below 1, or it never stops).

summary: Dotted-eighth delay (.delaysync(3/16)) is the dub spacing.
Feedback sets how long the echoes keep coming.
One delay per orbit: give the stab its own with .orbit(2).

lessons.title: The space
lessons.goal: Put the chord in a big room and thin the hats out of the low end.
lessons.concept:
Delay gives rhythm; **reverb** gives distance. Dub techno chords sit far back in a huge room, so turn `.room` up on the stab (it shares the stab's orbit, so it's the stab's own reverb).

As the effects pile up the low end gets muddy. A **high-pass filter** on the hats (`.hpf`) takes away lows they never needed, leaving room for the kick.

tasks.text: Give the stab a big reverb: room .6 or more.
High-pass the hats at 400 Hz or above.

challenge.text: Add a sine sub called sub on the root, an octave below the chord’s bass note, quiet.

summary: Reverb (.room) sets how far away a sound is.
High-pass the hats so the low end stays clear.
A quiet sine sub carries the root.

lessons.title: The movement
lessons.goal: Make the chord breathe over 16 bars, and add a clap and 16th hats.
lessons.concept:
Nothing in dub techno changes quickly, but everything changes. The classic move is the chord's filter **breathing**: opening and closing over 16 bars, so the same stab is never quite the same.

A **signal** does it: `sine.range(400, 1000).slow(16)` is a slow wave between 400 and 1000 Hz, one cycle every 16 bars. Give it to `.lpf` and the filter follows.

Then a little more rhythm: a soft clap on 2 and 4, and the hats on 16ths with a gain pattern, still quiet.

tasks.text: Replace the stab’s fixed cutoff with a 16-bar sine sweep between 400 and 1000 Hz.
Add a part called clap: a soft 909 clap on beats 2 and 4, in the stab’s room.
tasks.hint: const clap = s("~ cp ~ cp").bank("RolandTR909").gain(.5).room(.4).orbit(3), and stack it.

challenge.text: Turn the hats into 16ths with a gain pattern, still quiet.

summary: A slow signal on the filter makes the same chord breathe.
sine.range(a, b).slow(16): one sweep every 16 bars.
Each part with its own reverb gets its own orbit.

lessons.title: Project: The 12-inch
lessons.goal: Arrange the loop into a track: intro, main, a dub section, outro.
lessons.concept:
A 12-inch is a loop with a **shape**. Dub techno shapes are long and gentle: a drums-only **intro** a DJ can mix into, the **main** groove, a **dub** section where the kick drops out and the echoes carry the room, and a drums **outro**.

Sections are stacks with names; `arrange([8, intro], [16, main], …)` plays them in turn for that many bars each. Every section restarts its own clock, so the 16-bar sweep starts fresh with each section.

tasks.text: Name three sections: intro (kick and hats), main (everything) and outro (kick and hats). Keep playing main for now.
tasks.hint: const intro = stack(kick, hats), const main = stack(kick, hats, stab, clap), const outro = stack(kick, hats); end with main.

tasks.text: Arrange them: 8 bars of intro, 16 of main, 8 of outro.
tasks.hint: Replace the last line with arrange([8, intro], [16, main], [8, outro]).

challenge.text: Add an 8-bar dub section before the outro: no kick, just the stab, its echoes and the hats.
challenge.hint: const dub = stack(hats, stab), then arrange([8, intro], [16, main], [8, dub], [8, outro]).

summary: Sections are named stacks; arrange() plays them for so many bars each.
A drums-only intro and outro let a DJ mix the record.
A dub section drops the kick and lets the echoes carry the room.
